<!--
Word builds a table of contents from a field, and collects into it every
paragraph whose outline level is 1 to 3 -- which is every Heading 1 to 3 in
the document. apaquarto gives four of its own headings that style: the title,
the author note, the abstract and the impact statement. All four were listed,
none of them belong there, and a heading the writer marks {.unlisted} was
listed too. Each is written out with an outline level of 9, body text, which
the field passes over. The Heading style stays, so they look as they did.

The lists of figures and tables are apaquarto's own, and are built without a
field: ordinary paragraphs, each a link to the float it names. Nothing in
them needs updating, so Word shows them the moment the file opens, which is
the whole point of not using a field for them.
-->
